recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. The current core source already conveys the accepted resolution; adding a separate Device brand-name element or duplicating explanatory prose would conflict with or restate the current model.
issue_request: FHIR-28197 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Device change request asking whether Device needed a brand-name element, how to represent GUDID-style properties such as safety/radioactivity, and noting the misspelled DeviceDefinitionPropetyCode name. The accepted disposition was to avoid a new brand-name element, rely on FHIR-20639 name-type clarification for brand names, use Device.safety for the safety aspect, and fix the terminology/typo issue.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-28197 was found. The brand-name/name-type portion was applied through FHIR-20639 commits cae641cfad and c4a95b2b91, which replaced udi-label-name/manufacturer-name/model-name/other with registered-name, user-friendly-name, and patient-reported-name and updated Device/DeviceDefinition name-type summaries. The property and obsolete terminology surface was cleaned up through FHIR-26424 history.
additional_context: A May 2021 #devices Zulip thread for Device.deviceName.type discussed FHIR-28197 and identified GUDID brand name as the formal registered/labeler/manufacturer-assigned name. The 2021-09-27 OO HCP minutes list FHIR-28197 under Device.name and Device.safety with registered-name wording and the Device Safety value-set reference. Later FHIR-32812 removed open-ended old name-type values, FHIR-27765 introduced a distinct commercialBrand extension, and FHIR-47605 later added commercial-brand-family to the current core Device Name Type CodeSystem; those later related decisions are already represented on the combined branch where applicable.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Device and DeviceDefinition are active build resources. Current Device/DeviceDefinition source binds name-type elements to Device Name Type, whose registered-name definition covers manufacturer/labeler-assigned brand names, and also includes the later commercial-brand-family concept. Device.safety and DeviceDefinition.safety both bind to the Device Safety value set, and focused source checks found no old DeviceNameType codes or misspelled DeviceDefinition property-code names in active Device/DeviceDefinition source.
